DALLAS, September 11, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Generational Group, a leading mergers and acquisitions advisory firm for privately held businesses, is pleased to announce the sale of VOX Fulfillment LLC, a third-party logistics provider, to AMS Fulfillment, an omnichannel fulfillment company and portfolio company of Fort Point Capital. The acquisition closed on August 21, 2026.

Headquartered in Provo, Utah, VOX Fulfillment LLC supports growing e-commerce brands with fulfillment and logistics solutions designed to improve efficiency and reliability. From its 200,000-square-foot facility, the company manages more than 50,000 active SKUs and has fulfilled over 100 million orders for more than 1,000 brands.

VOX provides a broad range of fulfillment capabilities, allowing its customers to manage multiple aspects of their logistics through a single provider:

Order fulfillment and inventory management

Assembly and kitting

Global shipping across major carriers

E-commerce and marketplace integrations, including Shopify, Amazon, and Walmart

Reverse logistics and returns processing

Amazon FBM integration with A-to-Z Guarantee Claim coverage

These capabilities have enabled VOX to serve brands across the evolving e-commerce landscape while supporting their fulfillment needs as they grow.

Based in Valencia, California, AMS Fulfillment provides full-service outsourced logistics and omnichannel fulfillment services to fast-growing consumer products brands in the health and wellness, beauty and cosmetics, apparel, and consumer products sectors across retail, wholesale, and direct-to-consumer channels. Its network includes more than 1 million square feet of warehouse space across California, Delaware, and Pennsylvania, providing a broad operational footprint for its customers.

AMS processes more than 8.4 million orders and manages over 610,000 unique SKUs annually. The company has also built its platform around a combination of technology, service, and operational capabilities, including:

Comprehensive and scalable omni-channel fulfillment capabilities

High-touch support and customer service with a true partnership approach

Proprietary technology, including its WAMS warehouse management system and RateLogic shipping optimization tool

Advanced parcel-management capabilities

As a certified B Corporation, AMS incorporates environmental and social considerations into its operations while continuing to expand its fulfillment capabilities.

For Fort Point Capital, the transaction adds to a broader investment strategy focused on partnering with management of service-oriented middle market businesses to accelerate growth. The Boston-based private equity firm was founded in 2011 and brings a management-led, growth-oriented approach to private equity investing. Fort Point partners with founders and management teams to accelerate growth by providing resources to expand teams and infrastructure, improve service offerings, access new markets, and support follow-on acquisitions. Fort Point fulfills its commitment to management, employees and shareholders by employing a repeatable process to drive durable value, showcased in over 60 acquisitions since its inception.

Generational Group Executive Managing Director, M&A, Western Region – Lori Galloway, and her team, led by Senior Managing Director, M&A, Fred Zweifel successfully closed the deal. Senior Managing Director, Private Client Group, Eric Matuszak established the initial relationship with VOX Fulfillment LLC.

Ryan Binkley, CEO of Generational Group, stated, "We are pleased to have supported VOX Fulfillment through this important transaction. Our team is proud to have played a role in bringing the parties together and helping achieve a successful closing. We wish these organizations continued success as they move forward."

About Generational Group

Generational Group, headquartered in Dallas, TX, is a leading, award winning full-service M&A advisory firm. Generational has over 350 professionals across 17 offices in North America. The firm empowers business owners to unlock the full value of their companies through a comprehensive suite of services—including M&A advisory, exit planning education, business valuation, strategic growth advisory, wealth advisory, and digital solutions.

Celebrating its 21st year, Generational has successfully closed over 1,900 transactions and has ranked #1 or #2 in all LSEG league tables for deals valued between $25 million and $1 billion in 2024 and 2025.

title: YUM, WMT Stocks In Focus: CDC Declares Cyclospora Outbreak Over After Nearly 13,000 Cases
detail:
YUM, WMT Stocks In Focus: CDC Declares Cyclospora Outbreak Over After Nearly 13,000 Cases
YUM, WMT Stocks In Focus: CDC Declares Cyclospora Outbreak Over After Nearly 13,000 Cases · Stocktwits
Arnab Paul
Fri, September 11, 2026 at 9:53 AM PDT 2 min read
YUM
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The outbreak was linked to processed iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico.

Yum Brands-owned Taco Bell had sourced shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico and used it across stores in five states.

Taylor Farms recalled all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico on July 17.

Yum Brands (YUM) and Walmart (WMT) are in focus after U.S. health officials declared an end to a major Cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce that affected nearly 13,000 people.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said on Friday that the outbreak had ended after infections declined significantly and the affected lettuce disappeared from stores and restaurants. The outbreak resulted in 12,883 cases across 21 states, 570 hospitalizations and two deaths.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Cyclospora is a parasite that can contaminate food or water and cause an intestinal illness called cyclosporiasis. Symptoms include diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea, and fatigue.

Cyclospora Outbreak Traced To Mexico

According to investigations by the CDC, public health and regulatory officials in several states, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the outbreak was linked to processed iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico.

The earliest illness onset tied to the Cyclospora outbreak was May 13, while Taylor Farms recalled all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico on July 17. At its peak before the recall, more than 1,000 infections occurred in a single day. That fell to fewer than two per day on average in August, according to the CDC.

How YUM And WMT Are Tied To The Outbreak

According to the investigations, Yum Brands-owned Taco Bell had sourced shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico and used it across stores in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia. Taco Bell stopped using lettuce from the supplier on July 17.

Taylor Farms' recall also included iceberg salad and shredded lettuce products sold under Walmart's Marketside brand at select stores.

At the time of writing, YUM shares were down 1% and heading for their worst week in nearly two months. WMT stock was up 0.8%.

The CDC said all best-by dates for products linked to the outbreak have passed and there is currently no risk of contracting Cyclosporiasis from them. The FDA, however, is still investigating how the lettuce became contaminated with Cyclospora.

title: Should You Buy Walmart Stock After a 14% Decline in Six Months?
detail:
Should You Buy Walmart Stock After a 14% Decline in Six Months?
Vrishali Bagree
Fri, September 11, 2026 at 6:27 AM PDT 5 min read

^GSPC

COST
DG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart Inc. WMT shares have lost 14.3% over the past six months, reflecting a notable cooling in investor sentiment toward the retail giant. The decline is slightly narrower than the industry's 15% drop, but Walmart has sharply lagged the Zacks Retail – Wholesale sector's 0.5% dip and the S&P 500's 12.2% advance over the same period.

The divergence is striking because Walmart's operating performance remains solid, with continued market share gains and strong digital growth. The pullback appears to reflect a combination of near-term cost and consumer concerns, softer U.S. comparable sales growth and a still-demanding valuation rather than a breakdown in the company's long-term growth story.

Walmart has also lagged several prominent retail peers over the past three months. Shares of Target Corporation TGT have rallied 34.6 during the period, while Costco Wholesale Corporation COST and Dollar General Corporation DG have declined 10.2% and 9.5%, respectively.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Is Weighing on Walmart Stock?

Despite Walmart's resilient operating performance, several factors appear to be weighing on investor sentiment. A key concern is the increasingly challenging consumer backdrop. Management noted that shoppers, particularly those facing tighter household budgets, are making more deliberate spending choices amid elevated fuel costs and broader affordability pressures.

Walmart has responded by stepping up price investments and expanding rollbacks across categories. While this reinforces the company's value positioning and can support market share gains over time, aggressive pricing can pressure near-term margins before higher volumes fully offset the investment. Management itself noted that the benefits from lower prices can take time to materialize.

Another drag is the health and wellness business, where regulatory changes have created considerable top-line pressure. Pharmacy deflation and brand-to-generic transfers associated with maximum fair price regulation have weighed on Walmart U.S. comparable sales. At the same time, the sales benefit from GLP-1 drugs has moderated from previous years. Management emphasized that these issues are largely affecting reported sales growth rather than undermining the underlying profitability or long-term attractiveness of the health and wellness business.

Cost pressures are another issue. Higher fuel expenses, depreciation tied to elevated capital spending, healthcare costs and self-insurance expenses are limiting operating leverage. Walmart is also reinvesting tariff refunds into lower prices and customer experience, which should strengthen its competitive position but may temper near-term profit growth. These factors, combined with a softer consumer environment, could explain why investors remain cautious despite Walmart's otherwise healthy business momentum.

BBY's Three-Month Rally Meets Stronger Fundamentals

Best Buy's Q2 Beat Adds Weight to the Momentum

Higher memory costs are flowing into the assortment, creating elasticity risk even as Best Buy uses promotions, financing, trade-ins and earlier inventory purchases to preserve key price points.

Management expects computing growth to slow in the second half as comparisons get tougher. Traditional gaming also declined as Best Buy lapped the prior-year Switch 2 launch, underscoring the category's exposure to uneven product cycles.
